problem: VLN suffers from data scarcity that hurts generalization to unseen environments. Simulator-based augmentation is limited to specific scenes and Speaker instructions are uninformative, while web-collected images/videos are noisy and need heavy cleaning, and template instructions are inflexible.
motivation: Agents need diverse objects and spatial layouts plus well-aligned instructions to generalize. Foundation models (VLM, LLM, T2I) hold world knowledge that can rewrite existing human-annotated data into new observation-instruction pairs without any simulator or manual cleaning. Synthetic T2I data is noisy, so training must be designed to exploit it while limiting the noise.
key_idea: Rewrite human-annotated trajectories into unseen observation-instruction pairs by chaining a VLM, an LLM and a panoramic T2I model, then train with a two-stage mixing-then-focusing scheme with random observation cropping.
insight: Adding new objects to the scene descriptions before generating panoramas beats regenerating from the original descriptions (ablation No.4 vs No.1: Val Unseen SR 69.69 vs 67.52). LLM observation-contrast rewritten instructions beat Speaker instructions (No.2 67.43 vs speaker inst 65.05 SR on Val Unseen). Mixing more rewritten data does not help linearly, so training-side noise handling (final clean stage, random cropping) matters. About 3x the R2R data gives gains comparable to the ~350x larger ScaleVLN data on some metrics.
method: Scene description rewriting: Tag2Text (VLM) captions each original panoramic observation, then gpt-3.5-turbo-1106 with an in-context prompt adds plausible co-occurring objects and rephrases to highlight different objects, giving object-enriched descriptions.

Panorama-to-view generation: MultiDiffusion (30 inference steps) generates one panorama per rewritten description, and Equirec2Perspec discretizes it into 36 perspective views. This gives view consistency without stitching.
Sequential landmark grounding: an LLM extracts an ordered landmark list from the original instruction, and CLIP matches each ground-truth-action view to its most similar landmark (argmax similarity).

Observation-contrast instruction rewriting: the VLM describes the new ground-truth views. The LLM contrasts the grounded landmarks with the new descriptions, replaces landmarks accordingly and paraphrases action words, producing an aligned instruction I^r. Three new trajectories are made per original pair, each with one instruction.
Mixing-then-focusing training: Stage 1 mixes original and rewritten data, and Stage 2 continues on original data only to suppress noise. Rewritten data is used in both pretraining and finetuning.

Random observation cropping: in Stage 1, large patches are randomly cropped from different rewritten panoramas and recombined into new panoramas. This adds diversity and mitigates repeated-object artifacts of the T2I model.
Plug-in usage: applied to DUET (main) and HAMT, with PREVALENT data also used. For R2R-CE, DUET is pretrained on the discrete rewritten data and finetuned with a waypoint predictor.

setting.backbone: DUET (fine-tuned) with CLIP ViT-B/16 or ViT-L/14 features; augmentation data made by frozen Tag2Text, gpt-3.5-turbo-1106, MultiDiffusion and CLIP
setting.training_data: Original R2R/REVERIE/R4R human-annotated data + PREVALENT + RAM-rewritten data (14,025 pairs for R2R/R4R, 12,450 for REVERIE, i.e. 3x original); R2R-CE finetuning
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views); for R2R-CE, panorama with waypoint predictor candidates
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (R2R/REVERIE/R4R); predicted waypoints in continuous R2R-CE

results: With CLIP ViT-L/14, RAM improves DUET on R2R val-unseen from 73.22 to 76.29 SR and from 64.49 to 66.39 SPL, reaching 75 SR / 65 SPL on test-unseen, still below ScaleVLN (80 SR / 70 SPL). On REVERIE test-unseen it gets 57.44 SR and 25.77 RGSPL, beating AutoVLN and ScaleVLN. On R4R val-unseen it gets 55.28 SR vs 47.78 for PanoGen, and on R2R-CE val-unseen 44.15 SR vs 37.25 for DUET.
limitations: T2I generation is noisy (e.g. repeated objects) and has no explicit cross-step consistency, so the pipeline needs a clean second stage and random cropping.
Still below ScaleVLN on R2R with large-scale data, and the pipeline is costly (~30 h on 8 RTX 3090 GPUs for image generation plus LLM API calls).
Built mainly for discrete environments; the continuous setting is only transferred via pretraining.
